dedupe_keys.name: ozmin mineral deposits database and mineral deposits and mineral resources services

description: OZMIN is Geoscience Australia's relational database of geological and resource information for Australian mineral deposits, compiled from published references and designed so that attributes can be analysed with spatial data in a GIS. The national dataset holds over one thousand major and historically significant deposits for 60 mineral commodities, including coal. It is served live through the Mineral Deposits and Mineral Resources OGC web services (WFS and WMS) in EarthResourceML 2.0 and ERML Lite 1.0, with feature types for mines, mineral occurrences, mineral deposits, reserves and resources, commodities, mining activity, processing plants, major resource projects, mine waste and mine waste geochemistry. Older snapshot extracts (Release 3 of October 2000, as comma-delimited ASCII and Microsoft Access) are published by the Bioregional Assessment Programme on data.gov.au under CC-BY 3.0 Australia; the licence of the live services is not specified in their catalogue entry. Access is free. Caveats: the mapping services update weekly while downloads are snapshots, and the GA OZMIN web page returned 404 on 26 September 2026. For simulation it provides locations, commodities and resources of Australian mines and deposits, including mine waste, for asset inventories, supply risk and hazard exposure. Related catalogue records include the USGS MRDS and the Global Tailings Portal.
